find_in_mountain_array.optimal:
fetch(i): get(i) through a cache dict, so no index is fetched twice
find_peak:
    left = 0, right = length - 1
    while left < right:
        mid = (left + right) / 2
        if fetch(mid) < fetch(mid + 1): left = mid + 1, else: right = mid   (still climbing?)
    return left
search_slope(target, left, right, ascending):
    while left <= right:
        mid = (left + right) / 2, value = fetch(mid)
        if value == target: return mid
        go_right = (value < target) if ascending, else (value > target); move left or right
    return -1
peak = find_peak; search the rising slope [0, peak] first, then the falling slope [peak + 1, n - 1]

maximum_running_time_of_n_computers.brute:
remaining = copy of batteries, minutes = 0
loop:
    sort remaining largest first
    if fewer than n batteries or remaining[n - 1] == 0: return minutes
    for each i in 0..n-1: remaining[i] -= 1   (the n fullest each power one computer)
    minutes += 1
maximum_running_time_of_n_computers.optimal:
can_run(minutes):
    usable = sum over batteries of min(charge, minutes)   (a battery powers one computer at a time)
    return usable >= n * minutes
left = 0, right = sum of batteries / n
while left < right:
    mid = (left + right + 1) / 2   (round up: we keep the last feasible value)
    if can_run(mid): left = mid
    else: right = mid - 1
return left

kth_smallest_number_in_multiplication_ta.optimal:
if m > n: swap m and n
count_at_most(value):
    count = 0
    for each row in 1..m: count += min(n, value / row)   (entries of row that are <= value)
    return count
left = 1, right = m * n
while left < right:
    mid = (left + right) / 2
    if count_at_most(mid) >= k: right = mid
    else: left = mid + 1
return left

find_kth_smallest_pair_distance.optimal:
count_pairs_within(limit):   (nums is sorted)
    count = 0, left = 0
    for each right from 0 to n - 1:
        while nums[right] - nums[left] > limit: left += 1
        count += right - left   (every index in [left, right) pairs with right)
    return count
sort nums
left = 0, right = nums[n - 1] - nums[0]
while left < right:
    mid = (left + right) / 2
    if count_pairs_within(mid) >= k: right = mid
    else: left = mid + 1
return left

maximum_average_subarray_ii.optimal:
has_average_at_least(x):
    prefix = running sums of (value - x), starting at 0
    smallest_before = 0
    for each end from k to n:
        smallest_before = min(smallest_before, prefix[end - k])
        if prefix[end] - smallest_before >= 0: return true   (length >= k, average >= x)
    return false
left = min of nums, right = max of nums
while right - left > 1e-6:
    mid = (left + right) / 2
    if has_average_at_least(mid): left = mid
    else: right = mid
return left

size = length of merged
if size is odd: return merged[size / 2]
return (merged[size / 2 - 1] + merged[size / 2]) / 2
median_of_two_sorted_arrays.optimal:
value_at(arr, i) = arr[i], or -inf before the start, +inf past the end
shorter, longer = the two arrays with the shorter first
total = m + n, half = (total + 1) / 2
left = 0, right = length of shorter
while left <= right:
    i = (left + right) / 2, j = half - i   (i from shorter and j from longer form the left half)
    shorter_left = value_at(shorter, i - 1), shorter_right = value_at(shorter, i)
    longer_left = value_at(longer, j - 1), longer_right = value_at(longer, j)
    if shorter_left > longer_right: right = i - 1   (took too many from shorter)
    else if longer_left > shorter_right: left = i + 1
    else if total is odd: return max(shorter_left, longer_left)
    else: return (max(shorter_left, longer_left) + min(shorter_right, longer_right)) / 2

employee_free_time.brute:
nobody_works(gap_start, gap_end): no shift has start < gap_end and end > gap_start
all_shifts = every shift of every employee
gaps = empty list
for each shift first, for each shift second:
    gap_start = end of first, gap_end = start of second
    if gap_start < gap_end and nobody_works(gap_start, gap_end):   (a real, empty gap)
        add [gap_start, gap_end] to gaps if not already there
sort gaps
return gaps
employee_free_time.optimal:
heap = min-heap of (start, employee, position 0) over each employee's first shift   (k-way merge)
free = empty list
busy_until = none   (furthest end of busy time seen so far)
while the heap is not empty:
    pop (start, employee, position); end = that shift's end
    if busy_until exists and start > busy_until: append [busy_until, start] to free
    busy_until = max(busy_until, end)
    if employee has a shift at position + 1: push (its start, employee, position + 1)
return free

my_calendar_iii.brute:
init:
    events = empty list
book(start, end):
    append (start, end) to events
    best = 0
    for each (point, _) in events:
        covering = count of events (s, e) with s <= point < e   (max overlap sits at a start)
        best = max(best, covering)
    return best
my_calendar_iii.optimal:
init:
    change = empty dict time -> net change in open events there
book(start, end):
    change[start] += 1, change[end] -= 1
    best = 0, open_events = 0
    for each time in sorted keys of change:
        open_events += change[time]   (running total = events open at this time)
        best = max(best, open_events)
    return best

rectangle_area_ii.optimal:
covered_length(intervals):   (length of the union of y-intervals)
    total = 0, reach = none
    for each (start, end) in intervals sorted by start:
        if reach exists and start < reach: start = reach   (clip away the part already counted)
        if end > start: total += end - start, reach = end
    return total
events = (x1, enter, y1, y2) and (x2, leave, y1, y2) for each rectangle, sorted by x
active = empty list of y-intervals, area = 0, previous_x = x of the first event
for each (x, kind, y1, y2) in events:
    area += (x - previous_x) * covered_length(active)   (the strip left of x uses the old set)
    previous_x = x
    if kind is enter: add (y1, y2) to active, else: remove (y1, y2) from active
return area mod 1e9+7
